fix:gaps: Model-suggested companies are now checked only together with the person (affiliate) until a record that is not the model's reading shows they ran the company. This takes full effect once deepCheck.js and identity.js apply the changes listed for them.

fix:courts: Setting the CourtListener account value on the deployment turns on the fuller federal docket search, with parties, case numbers and state appellate opinions. The account is free and the site is non-commercial. Without it, only archive case titles are searched.

fix:courts: State trial courts (for example California and New York) have no free, permitted source and stay uncovered. Please decide whether the US Tax Court's public opinion search may be added once its terms have been checked.

fix:sec: Set SEC_USER_AGENT in Vercel (Production and Preview) to a name and contact email, for example 'Bivek Research ops@yourdomain.com'. An email in FOUNDER_HTTP_CONTACT also works. Without it, the SEC's website refuses every automated request, so filing texts (Form D roles, proxy passages), enforcement releases and SEC press releases are reported as not read.
fix:sec: That contact is sent to the SEC with each request to its website. Use a work or role address you are comfortable sharing with them.

fix:report: Records that match only the ordinary word a company is named with (boat ramp, The Ramp church, RAMP & CO LTD, Ethereum 'The Merge') are now out of the numbered report. They are counted and listed with a one-line reason in report.wordOnly. The page will show that list only once DeepCheck.js renders it.
fix:report: Clean screens in the brief now use the screen checklist's own source labels (for example 'Sanctions lists (US, UN, EU, UK, Canada)'), so the brief and the checklist always agree.

fix:quickbrief: The fair-use limits are a choice for you. Signed-out: 15 checks per 10 minutes and 40 per hour per address. Signed-in: 30 per 10 minutes and 120 per hour per account. All signed-out visitors together: 600 per hour. Change QUICK_LIMITS in src/pages/api/founder/index.js if you want other numbers.

fix:quickbrief: With no company typed, the quick brief now refuses to merge namesakes. Unless one organisation clearly dominates (at least 3 pages and 3 times the next), it asks which person is meant. Common names will see this choice more often.
fix:quickbrief: The counts are shared across server instances only on the hosted database (Neon). Locally they are kept in memory.

fix:knowledge: GitHub: the deployment may set GITHUB_TOKEN, a token with no scopes that costs nothing, for a larger hourly allowance. Without it, GitHub lookups share 60 requests an hour per network address, and each tied account now uses two extra requests (organisations and repositories).
fix:knowledge: Profiles now show a city from GitHub (the city only, nothing finer). Please confirm that is acceptable under the privacy rules; the audit said a city is allowed.
fix:knowledge: Wikidata 'member of' statements for political parties are deliberately left out. Say so if you want party membership shown.

fix:watchlists: The HHS OIG list now comes from the official monthly LEIE download (oig.hhs.gov, about 11 MB once a day) instead of the search page. Please confirm you are happy for the site to download this public file daily.

fix:watchlists: When the person's company was typed as a very large employer (for example Wells Fargo), a regulator record naming the same person at that employer now shows as 'likely', not 'confirmed'.

fix:security: Decide whether to set FOUNDER_ALLOWED_EMAILS in Vercel (production and preview), e.g. 'you@yourdomain.com' or '@yourdomain.com', separated by commas. Left empty, anyone with a Google account can still sign in and run checks as today. Set, everyone else is refused at sign-in, and their existing sessions stop working. The audit recommends setting it.
fix:security: With the list empty, production debug routes are open to any signed-in account, limited to 10 model runs an hour each. Setting the list restricts them to listed accounts.

fix:security: Preview deployments' debug routes still rely on the host's own preview sign-in being switched on in Vercel. Please confirm that protection is enabled; they are now limited to 10 model runs per caller and 40 per preview each hour either way.

fix:network: Seeding a check from a contact's company now needs the user's yes. Until the deep check route and page ask that question, a check started with no company is no longer seeded from a contact. That is deliberate, so a namesake cannot decide who the check is about.

fix:network: A contact whose title merely mentions an earlier company (for example 'ex-Theranos') is now listed as a possible former colleague. Ordinary-word names (Ramp, Merge) and very large organisations are never matched this way.

fix:loop: A company taken from your network (when no company is typed and one contact has the name) is still used automatically, but only as an assumption: records tied through it are likely at most and marked as such. The page could ask first; the API accepts useNetworkCompany:false. Decide whether the page should ask before every such check.

fix:loop: Watchlist, court and regulator screens may now go up to 15% past the 420-lookup budget, and up to 6 rounds past the round limit, so that they always run. Say if you want a different allowance.
fix:loop: FOUNDER_DEEP_PUBLIC=true now works only in local development and tests; it is ignored in production whatever the setting.

fix:registries: Patents are now off unless you set FOUNDER_GOOGLE_PATENTS=on. Google's terms bar automated querying and it turns automated callers away, and every other patent register (USPTO Open Data Portal, PatentsView, EPO) needs a registration. Decide whether to accept Google's terms risk, or register a free USPTO Open Data Portal account so a sanctioned connector can be built.

fix:registries: US trademarks are not enabled. The old route was the USPTO trademark web app's internal search, which the handover lists as removed for terms reasons. A permitted route would need a registered USPTO Open Data Portal account and a daily bulk-file cache. Decide whether you want that.

fix:registries: New registers to consider, each after a terms check: Australia's ASIC dataset, Corporations Canada open data, OpenCorporates (free non-commercial access on application, needs attribution). More breach registers: HHS OCR, and the Maine, Texas, Vermont, Indiana and Massachusetts attorneys general.

fix:identity2: Two choices here are stricter than before; tell us if you want them changed. A person known by one name ("Budi") is now only tied to a record when their company is named beside them. A record that names a very large employer (Google, Deloitte, HSBC, a university) next to the person stays "likely" until it also gives a second fact, such as a school or another company of theirs.
fix:identity2: A pardoned conviction is now graded medium, not high. The conviction still shows, with the pardon beside it once the report change lands.
fix:web: Google News stays on (as before). Press articles it finds are now matched to the publisher's own page through Bing News, at most 3 a check. No decoding of Google's links.

fix:web: Adverse searches now run in up to two local languages per person, chosen from a place or country given for them, the company's domain or the name's script. Each adds one web and one news lookup.
fix:web: The page reader now reads a company's legal name from its own website footer (for example 'Merge API, Inc.') and treats it as a known name of the company.

fix:web: A company named with an ordinary word (Ramp, Merge, Stripe, Flow) is never searched or matched on the bare word: a news item that only says 'Stripe' with no legal form, legal name, domain or founder's surname is no longer kept as a company record.

fix:profile: Leads are new on the Profile card: a name-only BrokerCheck registration whose dates fit a banking bio, and a name-only UK register directorship at a company whose name begins with theirs (for example RAMP BUSINESS UK LTD). Both are phrased as questions to confirm with the person, never as facts. Decide whether you want both kinds shown.
fix:profile: When a founder no longer holds a role at their company, the headline now reads, for example, 'Founder, Nikola (former CEO and Executive Chairman, until 2020)'.
